In 7-dimensional [[geometry]], the '''3<sub>21</sub>''' polytope is a [[uniform 7-polytope]], constructed within the symmetry of the [[E7 (mathematics)|E<sub>7</sub>]] group. It was discovered by [[Thorold Gosset]], published in his 1900 paper. He called it a [[Semiregular polytope|7-ic semi-regular figure]].<ref name=gosset>Gosset, 1900</ref>

Its [[Coxeter symbol]] is '''3<sub>21</sub>''', describing its bifurcating [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]], with a single ring on the end of one of the 3-node sequences.

The '''rectified 3<sub>21</sub>''' is constructed by points at the mid-edges of the '''3<sub>21</sub>'''. The '''birectified 3<sub>21</sub>''' is constructed by points at the triangle face centers of the '''3<sub>21</sub>'''. The '''trirectified 3<sub>21</sub>''' is constructed by points at the tetrahedral centers of the '''3<sub>21</sub>''', and  is the same as the rectified 1<sub>32</sub>.

These polytopes are part of a family of 127 (2<sup>7</sup>−1) convex [[Uniform 7-polytope|uniform polytopes in 7 dimensions]], made of [[uniform 6-polytope]] facets and [[vertex figure]]s, defined by all permutations of rings in this [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]]: {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}}.
{{clear}}

In 7-dimensional [[geometry]], the '''3<sub>21</sub>''' polytope is a [[uniform polytope]]. It has 56 vertices, and 702 facets: 126 [[hexacross|3<sub>11</sub>]] and 576 [[6-simplex]]es.

For visualization this 7-dimensional polytope is often displayed in a special skewed orthographic projection direction that fits its 56 vertices within an 18-gonal regular polygon (called a [[Petrie polygon]]). Its 756 edges are drawn between 3 rings of 18 vertices, and 2 vertices in the center. Specific higher elements (faces, cells, etc.) can also be extracted and drawn on this projection.

The 1-[[n-skeleton|skeleton]] of the '''3<sub>21</sub>''' polytope is the [[Gosset graph]].

This polytope, along with the [[7-simplex]], can [[Honeycomb (geometry)|tessellate]] 7-dimensional space, represented by [[3 31 honeycomb|'''3<sub>31</sub>''']] and Coxeter-Dynkin diagram: {{CDD||node|3|node|split1|nodes|3ab|nodes|3ab|nodes_10l}}.

=== Alternate names ===
*It is also called the '''Hess polytope''' for [[Edmund Hess]] who first discovered it.
*It was enumerated by [[Thorold Gosset]] in his 1900 paper. He called it a ''7-ic semi-regular figure''.<ref name=gosset />
*[[E. L. Elte]] named it V<sub>56</sub> (for its 56 vertices) in his 1912 listing of semiregular polytopes.{{sfnp|Elte|2006}}
*[[H. S. M. Coxeter|H.S.M. Coxeter]] called it '''3<sub>21</sub>''' due to its bifurcating [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]], having 3 branches of length 3, 2, and 1, and having a single ring on the final node of the 3 branch.
* Hecatonicosihexa-pentacosiheptacontahexa-exon (acronym: naq) - 126-576 facetted polyexon (Jonathan Bowers){{sfn|Klitzing|at=[https://bendwavy.org/klitzing/incmats/naq.htm (o3o3o3o *c3o3o3x - naq)]}}

=== Coordinates ===
The 56 vertices can be most simply represented in 8-dimensional space, obtained by the 28 permutations of the coordinates and their opposite:
: ± (−3, −3, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)

=== Construction ===
Its construction is based on the [[E7 (mathematics)|E7]] group. [[Coxeter]] named it as '''3<sub>21</sub>''' by its bifurcating [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]], with a single ring on the end of the 3-node sequence.

The facet information can be extracted from its [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]], {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1}}.

Removing the node on the short branch leaves the [[6-simplex]], {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1}}.

Removing the node on the end of the 2-length branch leaves the [[6-orthoplex]] in its alternated form: '''3<sub>11</sub>''', {{CDD|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1}}.

Every simplex facet touches a 6-orthoplex facet, while alternate facets of the orthoplex touch either a simplex or another orthoplex.

The [[vertex figure]] is determined by removing the ringed node and ringing the neighboring node. This makes '''[[Gosset 2 21 polytope|2<sub>21</sub>]]''' polytope, {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1}}.

Seen in a [[configuration (polytope)|configuration matrix]], the element counts can be derived by mirror removal and ratios of [[Coxeter group#Properties|Coxeter group]] orders.<ref>Coxeter, Regular Polytopes, 11.8 Gosset figures in six, seven, and eight dimensions, pp. 202–203</ref>

=== Related polytopes ===
The 3<sub>21</sub> is fifth in a dimensional series of [[Uniform k21 polytope|semiregular polytope]]s. Each progressive [[uniform polytope]] is constructed [[vertex figure]] of the previous polytope. [[Thorold Gosset]] identified this series in 1900 as containing all [[regular polytope]] facets, containing all [[simplex]]es and [[orthoplex]]es.
{{Gosset_semiregular_polytopes}}

It is in a dimensional series of uniform polytopes and honeycombs, expressed by [[Coxeter]] as 3<sub>''k''1</sub> series. (A degenerate 4-dimensional case exists as 3-sphere tiling, a tetrahedral [[hosohedron]].)
{{3_k1_polytopes}}

=== Alternate names ===
* Rectified hecatonicosihexa-pentacosiheptacontahexa-exon as a rectified 126-576 facetted polyexon (acronym: ranq) (Jonathan Bowers){{sfn|Klitzing|at=[https://bendwavy.org/klitzing/incmats/ranq.htm (o3o3o3o *c3o3x3o - ranq)]}}

=== Construction ===
Its construction is based on the [[E7 (mathematics)|E7]] group. [[Coxeter]] named it as '''3<sub>21</sub>''' by its bifurcating [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]], with a single node on the end of the 3-node sequence.

The facet information can be extracted from its [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]], {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1|3a|nodea}}.

Removing the node on the short branch leaves the [[6-simplex]], {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1|3a|nodea}}.

Removing the node on the end of the 2-length branch leaves the [[rectified 6-orthoplex]] in its alternated form: '''t<sub>1</sub>3<sub>11</sub>''', {{CDD|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1|3a|nodea}}.

Removing the node on the end of the 3-length branch leaves the [[2 21 polytope|2<sub>21</sub>]], {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1}}.

The [[vertex figure]] is determined by removing the ringed node and ringing the neighboring node. This makes [[5-demicube]] prism, {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea_1|2|nodea_1}}.

=== Alternate names ===
* Birectified hecatonicosihexa-pentacosiheptacontahexa-exon as a birectified 126-576 facetted polyexon (acronym: branq) (Jonathan Bowers){{sfn|Klitzing|at=[https://bendwavy.org/klitzing/incmats/branq.htm (o3o3o3o *c3x3o3o - branq)]}}

=== Construction ===
Its construction is based on the [[E7 (mathematics)|E7]] group. [[Coxeter]] named it as '''3<sub>21</sub>''' by its bifurcating [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]], with a single node on the end of the 3-node sequence.

The facet information can be extracted from its [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]], {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea_1|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}}.

Removing the node on the short branch leaves the [[birectified 6-simplex]], {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}}.

Removing the node on the end of the 2-length branch leaves the [[birectified 6-orthoplex]] in its alternated form: '''t<sub>2</sub>(3<sub>11</sub>)''', {{CDD|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea_1|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}}.

Removing the node on the end of the 3-length branch leaves the [[rectified 2 21 polytope|rectified 2<sub>21</sub> polytope]] in its alternated form: '''t<sub>1</sub>(2<sub>21</sub>)''', {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea_1|3a|nodea}}.

The [[vertex figure]] is determined by removing the ringed node and ringing the neighboring node. This makes [[rectified 5-cell]]-triangle duoprism, {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch_10|2|nodea_1|3a|nodea}}.
